answer: The BLIS configuration space Pareto front has 35 unique objective vectors among 124 non-dominated configs out of 1800 total. The space has bimodal structure: single-instance configs (saturated) where all 6 knobs interact via KV-cache threshold effects, and multi-instance configs (unconstrained) where only tp and num_instances matter. TP is the dominant knob (1.5-1.8x throughput per doubling); KV blocks have sharp threshold effects; scheduler and block_size are secondary. A structured phased search exploiting this regime knowledge achieves 100% coverage of unique Pareto objective vectors using 200 evaluations (11.1% of the space), completing in ~25 seconds.
